newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA OTC PLANS 2,000 LISTINGS AT END-1996.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA OTC PLANS 2,000 LISTINGS AT END-1996.

text.p: Romania's budding over-the- counter (OTC) market boasts over 1,000 listings and hopes to double that number by the end of the year, an official said on Wednesday.
The market aims to reach 3,000 listings late in January.
"The 1,000-stock threshold is behind us, with the OTC listing 1,207 stocks now," Stefan Boboc, president of market regulator CNVM, told a news conference marking the event.
Romania's RASDAQ system opened late in October with six stocks and a first-week turnover of 9.0 million lei. Last week's five trading days yielded 795 million lei in turnover.

The RASDAQ opened under a U.S. Agency for International Development capital market project. It is scheduled eventually to trade 5,000 companies, most of them privatised under a mass selloff which gave Romanians shares in exchange for coupons.

Under recent CNVM rules, companies privatised under the mass selloff have to sign up with the Romanian shareholders' registry (RRA) -- created to accommodate these companies -- and then get an OTC listing.
Bourse officials disapproved of the rules, saying they were pushing companies onto the OTC market.
"To get a bourse listing takes a long time. In the meantime, the OTC offers these companies a market for their shares," said RRA general manager Mircea Ilie.
"When they are good and ready companies can move away from the OTC market and into the stock exchange, with the RRA making the transfer to the bourse's registry in 10 days."

The Bucharest bourse opened in November 1995 and now trades 17 stocks. Trading has been sluggish of late, with officials and brokers quoting share liquidity shortages as one of the reasons for the modest volumes. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
